option_relations.rationale: Acute tubular necrosis is a key component of the acute kidney injury described in the leaf, which is itself a manifestation of the overall condition.

The patient has pre-existing diabetes and the renal biopsy shows diffuse nodular diabetic glomerulosclerosis, indicating chronic diabetic nephropathy. The acute kidney injury is occurring in the context of this pre-existing condition, which is part of the broader clinical picture described in the leaf.
Diabetic nephropathy is a chronic condition present in the patient (evidenced by nodular diabetic glomerulosclerosis on biopsy) and contributes to the overall renal pathology described in the leaf.

Acute oxalate nephropathy is explicitly mentioned as a component of the leaf diagnosis ('Ethylene glycol poisoning with acute oxalate nephropathy and acute kidney injury'). The biopsy findings of multifocal oxalate crystal deposits directly support this.
